samuel1.16.p1.b1.text: How long are you going to mourn for Saul … Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem, for I have selected from his sons a king for Myself.

samuel1.16.p1.b2.text: How can I go? … Saul will hear of it and kill me!

samuel1.16.p1.b3.text: Take a heifer with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’

samuel1.16.p2.b1.text: So Samuel did what the LORD had said and went to Bethlehem. When the elders of the town met him, they trembled …

samuel1.16.p2.b3.text: In peace … I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.

samuel1.16.p2.b4.text: Then he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.

samuel1.16.p3.b1.text: Surely here before the LORD is His anointed.

samuel1.16.p3.b2.text: Do not consider his appearance or height, for I have rejected him; the LORD does not see as man does. For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.

samuel1.16.p4.b1.text: The LORD has not chosen this one either.

samuel1.16.p4.b2.text: The LORD has not chosen this one either.

samuel1.16.p4.b3.text: Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel …

samuel1.16.p4.b4.text: The LORD has not chosen any of these.

samuel1.16.p5.b1.text: Are these all the sons you have?

samuel1.16.p5.b2.text: There is still the youngest … but he is tending the sheep.

samuel1.16.p5.b3.text: Send for him … For we will not sit down to eat until he arrives.

samuel1.16.p5.b4.text: Rise and anoint him, for he is the one.

samuel1.16.p6.b1.text: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers …

samuel1.16.p6.b2.text: … the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward.

samuel1.16.p6.b3.text: Then Samuel set out and went to Ramah.

samuel1.16.p7.b1.text: After the Spirit of the LORD had departed from Saul, a spirit of distress from the LORD began to torment him.

samuel1.16.p7.b2.text: … seek out someone who can skillfully play the harp. … he is to play it, and you will be well.

samuel1.16.p7.b3.text: I have seen a son of Jesse of Bethlehem who knows how to play the harp. He is a mighty man of valor, a warrior, eloquent and handsome, and the LORD is with him.

samuel1.16.p8.b1.text: And Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine, and one young goat, and sent them to Saul with his son David.

samuel1.16.p8.b2.text: Saul admired him greatly, and David became his armor-bearer.

samuel1.16.p8.b3.text: … David would pick up his harp and play, and Saul would become well, and the spirit of distress would depart from him.
